title: Submit a batch, then join it

blocks.text: The page contrasts the ways to hand a task to a pool: `invoke(task)` **blocks** until the task is done, while `submit(task)` returns a `ForkJoinTask<V>` (a `Future`) **at once**, and you call `join()` or `get()` later to collect the result.
Write `Batch.runAll(pool, tasks)`. It hands **every** task to **`pool`** with `submit` before it waits for any of them, then joins them and returns their results in the order of the list.

rows: a task returning `"alpha"`, then one returning `"beta"` once alpha is done
two tasks that each wait until the other has started
three tasks that note the pool they run in

blocks.text: Calling `pool.invoke(task)` for each task in turn would run them one after the other: a task that needs another one running beside it would then never finish.
Note that `task.fork()` called from a thread outside any pool pushes the task to the **common** pool, not to `pool`.

cases.says: Each task's result comes back, in the order of the list.
All tasks are submitted before the first join, so they can run at the same time.
Every task runs in the pool that was passed in, not in the common pool.
Two tasks with equal results give two entries: one result per task, nothing merged.
When the second task finishes first, the results are still in list order.

concepts: submit(task) returns a ForkJoinTask future at once, so several tasks can be submitted before any is joined.
